summary:
We built ACCENSIO, a live fire safety simulator and risk dashboard for spacecraft cabins, trained on open NASA Physical Sciences Informatics datasets (PSI-25, PSI-100, and PSI-102). Our web app connects a microgravity combustion physics visualizer to a FastAPI machine learning backend and a Gemini-powered assistant.

Fire behaves completely differently in zero gravity. Without buoyancy, flames can burn as quiet, near-invisible blue spheres in stagnant air, or suddenly turn into fast-moving blowtorches when cabin ventilation fans and oxygen levels go up. ACCENSIO lets operators test how different cabin materials react to airflow, oxygen enrichment, and hidden wire smoldering. It calculates real-time ignition probabilities across five station compartments, ranks which room needs attention first, and tells the crew the exact steps to stabilize the cabin like dialing down local fans or scrubbing carbon monoxide.

As longer missions head to the Moon and Mars, astronauts need predictive tools that catch invisible pyrolysis and airflow hazards early, rather than just waiting for a standard smoke alarm to go off.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

We built ACCENSIO, a live fire safety simulator and risk dashboard for spacecraft cabins. When we started researching for this challenge, we were surprised to learn that fire in space doesn't behave anything like fire on Earth. Without gravity pulling hot air up, flames can float as quiet, near-invisible blue balls in still air, or suddenly stretch into fast-moving blowtorches if a cabin fan blows on them or oxygen levels rise.

To solve this, we built an interactive web app where users can adjust cabin oxygen, fan airflow, carbon monoxide (CO), and carbon dioxide across five different space station rooms (like the Destiny Lab and Avionics Bay) and test five real spacecraft materials, including Kapton wire insulation and PMMA acrylic.

Our app runs on two main parts:

  • The Physics & Machine Learning Backend: We trained a Random Forest model using real open-science data from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database (specifically the BASS-II, SAFFIRE-3, and SAME microgravity fire experiments). Our Python FastAPI server calculates the real-time probability of a fire spreading and figures out what steps the crew should take to stop it.
  • The Live Simulator & AI Helper: We coded a custom animation on HTML5 Canvas that shows the flame changing shape right in front of you as you move the sliders. We also connected Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash so users can ask questions about microgravity fire safety and get answers based on the live room settings.

Why It Matters & Intended Impact Regular smoke alarms on Earth rely on smoke rising to the ceiling, which doesn't happen in zero gravity. In space, electrical wires can smolder behind panels and release carbon monoxide long before anyone sees a flame. ACCENSIO helps catch those hidden warning signs early. Instead of just flashing a warning light, our dashboard ranks all five station rooms by danger level and tells the crew the exact fix—like turning down a specific fan or scrubbing CO from the air—with a one-click auto-stabilizer button. As astronauts prepare for longer trips to the Moon and Mars, having smart tools like this can keep crews much safer.

Tools & Tech We Used

  • Backend & AI: Python, FastAPI, Scikit-Learn (Random Forest model), NumPy, Pandas, and the Google GenAI SDK (gemini-2.5-flash).
  • Frontend & Visuals: HTML5 Canvas (for the flame and airflow simulation), CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Data & Hosting: NASA Open Science PSI Datasets (PSI-25, PSI-100, PSI-102), GitHub, Render (for our backend API), and Netlify (for our website).

Creativity & What We Considered

We wanted to make tough aerospace physics easy to understand at a glance. Instead of just showing numbers in a table, we designed the live flow chamber so you can visually see how turning up the airflow turns a calm blue flame into an orange blowtorch. While building it, we also realized a crew wouldn't just monitor one room at a time, so we programmed the app to remember custom slider settings for every compartment independently and rank the whole station at once.
